properties.chose:
ACCEPTED on @ajs's word, 2026-10-13, ruling on the judgement pass's short list (item 1): "Write down the few jobs reflow2 does, as the yardstick for every later cut." Option (a). His 2026-10-13 direction already answers whether to prune (do fewer things, let borderline ones go gradually). What this adds is the yardstick: a short list, in a person's words, of the few jobs reflow2 does, against which each later cut is measured. The list itself is his to write; until it exists, no cut is measured against it. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq

THE FEW JOBS, WRITTEN 2026-10-13 on @ajs's word. Claude drafted them; he changed jobs 1 and 3 after reading his own research on how models are evolving. His words: "the new wording for jobs 1 and 3 are right". THE YARDSTICK FOR EVERY LATER CUT: anything reflow2 does that serves none of these is a candidate to let go, and anything new must serve one.
1. Keep one shared record of what was decided, by whom and why, across every model, person and agent.
2. Before you change something, show what else it touches.
3. Find what's structurally missing or contradictory, with checks that don't reason and can't be talked round, and ask you in plain questions.
4. Show whether what was built meets what was asked, by checks anyone can re-run.
5. Keep your decisions yours: nothing you intended changes without your word, and you can see what the agent filled in.
Why 1 and 3 changed: model memory and model reasoning will keep improving, but vendor memory is per model, per person and not auditable, and a model's judgement is not a check. So reflow2 keeps the shared, attributable record and the checks that do not reason, and leaves remembering and judging to the model. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex's feedback, relayed by @ajs on 2026-09-28: "reflow2 shouldn't try to do everything, but instead focus on doing the things it does well and doing them really well." @ajs names the yardstick: "Reflow2 was created so that a user can design something without knowing systems engineering and proper design practices. This is its core identity." That is req:no-se-knowledge (accepted): "The graph carries the discipline; the user answers plain questions."

WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY MEASURED (not re-measured for this record):
- fact:reflow2-keeps-reflows-spirit-and-inherits-its-one-real-drift (2026-09-13): reflow2 is faithful in spirit, but has drifted the one way reflow did, toward itself. 80% of recorded tool calls are self-host; 181 tools were served, 40 never called, and only one was ever retired; 249 of 254 verifications have no executable form; the delivery is software-shaped under neutral nouns.
- dec:idea-prune-the-tool-surface-to-an-orthogonal-essential-set (2026-09-17/18): 61 mutually confusable tool pairs; the three prunable kinds would take 186 → 170. The surface is 193 today.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) NAME THE FEW JOBS, IN A PERSON'S WORDS, and hold everything to them. Reflow2 exists to do a short list of things for someone who knows no systems engineering, for example:
  - turn what I want into a design I can read back;
  - tell me what I haven't decided, and ask me plainly;
  - keep what I build matching what I designed;
  - remember why.
  Every tool, skill and detector would then say which job it serves, and one that serves none becomes a candidate to park. Cheap to write down; choosing the list is the hard part, and it is @ajs's.
(b) PARK WHAT SERVES NO JOB: behind a flag, or off the served surface. Never deleted, because history stays. Medium; depends on (a).
(c) SPLIT BY AUDIENCE: a small default surface for a designer's agent, with the rest (release cuts, hosting, self-host instruments, federation) served only on request. This is the prune idea's option D. Medium.
(d) NOTHING NEW: keep adding, and rely on find_tools and the skills to hide the size.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
· The discipline has to live somewhere. "The graph carries the discipline" means the engine is SUPPOSED to hold a lot of systems engineering (detectors, traceability, epochs) so the person does not. Size inside the engine is not drift. Size that REACHES the person is: tools a chat model must choose among, jargon in a reply, a question only an engineer can answer.
· Some breadth is how a non-expert reaches reflow2 at all: flo2's hosting, the remote client, the chat doors. Cutting those in the name of focus would narrow who can use it, the opposite of the identity.
· Parking costs something. A tool nobody sees is a tool nobody calls (the unreachable half of dec:bl-155), and the detector and the instruction still have to point at whatever stays.
· The drift measured so far is mostly SELF-ABSORPTION: reflow2 building instruments for reflow2. "Do fewer things" fixes that only if the list in (a) is applied to reflow2's own upkeep work as well as to its features.

2026-09-28, LATER THE SAME DAY: the core identity quoted above is one clause short. docs/vision.md, the north star since the first commit (2026-07-17), states it as: "Someone with only an idea is guided — by questions — from concept to operations without needing to know systems engineering." Anthony confirmed the whole-lifecycle scope the same day (dec:idea-reflow2-serves-a-design-in-operations-where-incidents-feed-the-design, accepted): "I've designed reflow2 from the beginning to be the complete lifecycle from concept to operations/fielding." So any list of the few jobs in option (a) is measured against concept → operations, not against the design phase alone. The short quote is how a triage framed operations as a possible expansion (fact:root-cause-the-lifecycle-scope-lives-in-the-vision-and-the-graph-holds-one-line-so-a-brainstorm-reopened-it-2026-09-28).

properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill (fetched fresh). The design was searched before writing, and the prior measurement is cited rather than repeated. Kept separate from the review question (dec:idea-review-reflow2-against-its-core-identity-and-how-it-delivers-on-it), because this one asks what reflow2 should STOP doing and that one asks how to find out.
